summary: Menachos and nesachim that became tamei can be redeemed only before they became holy in a holy vessel. Birds, wood, frankincense and holy vessels can never be redeemed, because redeeming is said only about animals.

chunks.en: Menachos and nesachim that became tamei, before
chunks.st: With regard to the fine flour for meal offerings or the wine for libations that became ritually impure,

chunks.en: he made them holy in the vessel,
chunks.st: as long as they have not yet been consecrated in a service vessel and assumed inherent sanctity,

chunks.en: can be redeemed.
chunks.explain: Their holiness can be moved onto money.
chunks.st: their redemption is possible.
chunks.stMore: If they are redeemed, their sanctity will be transferred to the redemption money.

chunks.en: Once they became holy in the vessel,
chunks.st: Once they have been consecrated in a service vessel and have assumed inherent sanctity,

chunks.en: they cannot be redeemed.
chunks.st: their redemption is no longer possible, and they are burned like any other offerings that became ritually impure.

chunks.en: Birds, wood, frankincense and holy vessels
chunks.st: With regard to consecrated birds, wood for the altar, frankincense, and service vessels,

chunks.en: cannot be redeemed,
chunks.st: once they became ritually impure they have no possibility of redemption,

chunks.en: because it was said only about an animal.
chunks.st: as redemption of items consecrated for the altar was stated only with regard to a consecrated animal that developed a blemish, not with regard to other consecrated items.

summary: If someone promised a mincha in one kind of pan or in one vessel, and brought it in another way, it counts as a gift but he still owes his promise. If he said "this flour" and changed it, it is pasul. The mishnah also teaches what happens if people reminded him of his promise.

chunks.en: If someone says, "I take upon myself a mincha in a flat pan,"
chunks.st: In the case of one who says: It is incumbent upon me to bring a meal offering prepared in a shallow pan,

chunks.en: and he brought it in a deep pan,
chunks.st: and he brought a meal offering prepared in a deep pan instead;

chunks.en: or "in a deep pan," and he brought it in a flat pan,
chunks.st: or if he said: It is incumbent upon me to bring a meal offering prepared in a deep pan, and he brought a meal offering prepared in a shallow pan instead,

chunks.en: what he brought, he brought,
chunks.explain: It counts as a gift mincha.
chunks.st: the meal offering that he brought, he brought as a voluntary meal offering,

chunks.en: but he did not keep his promise.
chunks.st: but he has not fulfilled his obligation that he undertook with his vow and he must therefore bring another meal offering.

chunks.en: If he said, "This is to be brought in a flat pan,"
chunks.st: If he said: This tenth of an ephah of flour is a meal offering to bring in a shallow pan,

chunks.en: and he brought it in a deep pan,
chunks.st: and he brought it prepared in a deep pan instead;

chunks.en: or "in a deep pan," and he brought it in a flat pan,
chunks.st: or if he said: This tenth of an ephah of flour is a meal offering to bring in a deep pan, and he brought a meal offering prepared in a shallow pan,

chunks.en: this one is pasul.
chunks.st: this offering is not valid, because he did not fulfill what he had stated concerning that tenth of an ephah of flour.

chunks.en: "I take upon myself two issaron
chunks.st: In the case of one who says: It is incumbent upon me to bring one meal offering of two tenths of an ephah

chunks.en: to bring in one vessel,"
chunks.st: in one vessel, and he

chunks.en: and he brought it in two vessels;
chunks.st: divided it and brought it in two vessels, removing a handful from each;

chunks.en: or "in two vessels,"
chunks.st: or if he says: It is incumbent upon me to bring two tenths of an ephah for two meal offerings in two vessels,

chunks.en: and he brought it in one vessel,
chunks.st: and he brought one meal offering of two tenths of an ephah in one vessel and removed one handful from it,

chunks.en: what he brought, he brought,
chunks.st: then the meal offering that he brought, he brought as a voluntary meal offering,

chunks.en: but he did not keep his promise.
chunks.st: but he has not fulfilled his obligation.

chunks.en: "These are to be brought in one vessel,"
chunks.st: If he says: These two tenths of an ephah before me are a meal offering in one vessel, and he

chunks.en: and he brought them in two vessels;
chunks.st: divided them and brought them in two vessels, removing a handful from each;

chunks.en: or "in two vessels," and he brought them in one vessel,
chunks.st: or if he says: These tenths of an ephah are two meal offerings in two vessels, and he brought them in one vessel,

chunks.en: these are pasul.
chunks.st: both of these offerings are not valid, because in both cases he deviated from the number of handfuls that he vowed to remove.

chunks.en: "I take upon myself two issaron to bring
chunks.st: In the case of one who says: It is incumbent upon me to bring a meal offering of two tenths of an ephah

chunks.en: in one vessel," and he brought them in two vessels,
chunks.st: in one vessel, and he divided them and brought them in two vessels,

chunks.en: and people said to him, "You promised one vessel":
chunks.st: and others said to him: You vowed to bring a meal offering in one vessel,

chunks.he: הִקְרִיבָן בִּכְלִי אֶחָד, כְּשֵׁרִים, וּבִשְׁנֵי כֵלִים, פְּסוּלִין.
chunks.en: if he brought them in one vessel, they are kosher, and in two vessels, they are pasul.
chunks.st: then if he sacrificed the two tenths of an ephah in two vessels they are not valid even as voluntary meal offerings, and he must bring another meal offering to fulfill his obligation. His failure to respond and explain that it was not his intention to fulfill his vow with this offering indicates that he does intend to fulfill his vow with it. Since he deviated from his vow, the offering is not valid. If he sacrificed the two tenths of an ephah in one vessel after he was reminded, it is valid, as he fulfilled his vow.

chunks.en: "I take upon myself two issaron
chunks.st: Likewise, in a case where one says: It is incumbent upon me to bring two meal offerings totaling two tenths of an ephah

chunks.en: to bring in two vessels,"
chunks.st: in two vessels,

chunks.en: and he brought them in one vessel,
chunks.st: and he brought it all in one vessel,

chunks.en: and people said to him,
chunks.st: and others said to him:

chunks.en: "You promised two vessels":
chunks.st: You vowed to bring meal offerings in two vessels,

chunks.en: if he brought them in two vessels,
chunks.st: then if he sacrificed the two tenths of an ephah in two vessels

chunks.en: they are kosher. If he put it in one vessel,
chunks.st: as he had originally vowed, they are valid. If he placed it all in one vessel,

chunks.en: it is like two menachos that got mixed.
chunks.st: its halakhic status is like that of two meal offerings that were intermingled prior to removal of the handfuls.
chunks.stMore: Therefore, if one can remove a handful from each meal offering in and of itself, they are valid. If not, they are not valid, as the Gemara explained on 23a.

summary: If someone promised a mincha in a way that menachos are not brought (from barley, plain flour, without oil, or half an issaron), he must bring a proper one. Rabbi Shimon says he does not need to bring anything, because that is not how people promise.

chunks.en: "I take upon myself a mincha from barley":
chunks.st: One who says: It is incumbent upon me to bring a meal offering from barley,

chunks.en: he must bring it from wheat.
chunks.st: should bring the meal offering from wheat, as voluntary meal offerings are brought exclusively from wheat.

chunks.en: "Plain flour": he must bring fine flour.
chunks.st: One who says: It is incumbent upon me to bring a meal offering from flour, should bring the meal offering from fine flour, as it is written: “His offering shall be of fine flour” (Leviticus 2:1).

chunks.en: "Without oil and frankincense":
chunks.st: If one vows to bring a meal offering without oil and without frankincense,

chunks.en: he must bring oil and frankincense with it.
chunks.st: he should bring it with oil and frankincense, as voluntary meal offerings require oil and frankincense.

chunks.en: "Half an issaron":
chunks.st: If one vows to bring as a meal offering half a tenth of an ephah,

chunks.en: he must bring a whole issaron.
chunks.st: he should bring a complete tenth of an ephah, the minimum measure of a voluntary meal offering.

chunks.en: "An issaron and a half":
chunks.st: If one vows to bring a meal offering of a tenth and a half an ephah,

chunks.en: he must bring two.
chunks.st: he should bring two tenths, as there are no partial tenths of an ephah brought in meal offerings.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says he does not have to bring anything,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon deems one exempt from bringing a meal offering in all these cases.
chunks.stMore: This is because the vow does not take effect,

chunks.en: because he did not promise the way people promise.
chunks.st: as he did not pledge in the manner of those who pledge.

summary: A person may give a mincha of up to sixty issaron in one vessel; if he promised sixty-one, he brings sixty in one vessel and one in another, because the community brings at most sixty-one in one day. Rabbi Shimon says the reason is that only sixty can be mixed with oil, like the forty se'ah of a mikveh. The mishnah also lists which amounts of wine may be given.

chunks.he: מִתְנַדֵּב אָדָם מִנְחָה שֶׁל שִׁשִּׁים עִשָּׂרוֹן,
chunks.en: A person may give a mincha of sixty issaron
chunks.st: A person may pledge a meal offering of sixty tenths of an ephah of fine flour,

chunks.en: and bring it in one vessel.
chunks.st: and bring all sixty tenths in one vessel. If he says: It is incumbent upon me to bring sixty tenths of an ephah, he brings it in one vessel.

chunks.he: אִם אָמַר הֲרֵי עָלַי שִׁשִּׁים וְאֶחָד,
chunks.en: If he said, "I take upon myself sixty-one,"
chunks.st: If he says: It is incumbent upon me to bring sixty-one tenths of an ephah,

chunks.en: he brings sixty in one vessel
chunks.st: he brings sixty tenths in one vessel

chunks.en: and one in another vessel,
chunks.st: and one tenth in another vessel,

chunks.en: because the community brings
chunks.st: as the greatest number of tenths of an ephah that the community brings as meal offerings in one day is

chunks.en: on the first day of Sukkos
chunks.st: on the first festival day of Sukkot when it

chunks.en: that falls on Shabbos, sixty-one.
chunks.st: occurs on Shabbat, when sixty-one tenths of an ephah of fine flour are brought.

chunks.he: דַּיּוֹ לַיָּחִיד שֶׁיְּהֵא פָחוֹת מִן הַצִּבּוּר אֶחָד.
chunks.en: It is enough for one person to be one less than the community.
chunks.st: It is sufficient for an individual that the maximum amount he can bring at once is one tenth of an ephah less than that of the community.
chunks.stMore: When the first day of Sukkot occurs on Shabbat, thirteen bulls, two goats, and fourteen lambs are sacrificed as the additional offerings of Sukkot, two lambs are sacrificed as the daily offerings, and two lambs are sacrificed as the additional offering of Shabbat. Three tenths of an ephah are brought for each bull, two tenths for each goat, and a tenth for each lamb. Altogether, that is sixty-one tenths of an ephah.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon said:
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:
chunks.stMore: What is the relevance of the tenths of an ephah sacrificed on Sukkot that occurs on Shabbat?

chunks.en: But aren't these for the bulls,
chunks.st: Aren’t these meal offerings for bulls

chunks.en: and those for the lambs,
chunks.st: and those for lambs,

chunks.en: and they are not mixed with each other?
chunks.st: and they are not mixed with each other (see 89a)?

chunks.en: Rather, up to sixty issaron can be mixed together.
chunks.explain: Mixed with one log of oil.
chunks.st: Rather, the reason that one may not bring more than sixty tenths of an ephah in one vessel is because up to sixty tenths of fine flour can be mixed with one log of oil.

chunks.en: They said to him:
chunks.st: The Rabbis said to him:

chunks.en: Sixty can be mixed,
chunks.st: Is it so that sixty tenths of flour can be mixed with a log of oil,

chunks.en: but sixty-one cannot be mixed?
chunks.st: but sixty-one tenths cannot be mixed?

chunks.en: He said to them:
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon said to them:

chunks.en: All the measures of the Sages are like this.
chunks.st: All the measures of the Sages are so:

chunks.en: In forty se'ah of water he can toviel,
chunks.st: For example, in a ritual bath containing forty se’a of water, one immerses for purification,

words.note: Dips in a mikveh to become tahor.

chunks.en: but in forty se'ah missing a tiny bit
chunks.st: and in a ritual bath with forty se’a less the small measure of a kortov,

chunks.en: he cannot toviel in it.
chunks.st: one cannot immerse in it for purification.

chunks.en: They do not give one log of wine,
chunks.st: One does not pledge a libation of one log,

chunks.en: or two, or five,
chunks.st: two log, or five log of wine, because there are no existing libations with those measures of wine.

chunks.en: but they may give three, four, or six,
chunks.st: But one pledges a libation of three log, which is the measure of wine brought with a lamb, or four log, which is the measure of wine brought with a ram, or six log, which is the measure of wine brought with a bull.

chunks.en: or from six and up.
chunks.st: And one may pledge a libation of six log and beyond, as any greater amount can be composed of combinations of these three.

summary: Rabbi Akiva says a person may give wine by itself but not oil; Rabbi Tarfon says oil too, and they argue. Two people may not share one issaron mincha, but they may share an olah or shelamim, and a person may give even one bird.

chunks.en: They may give wine,
chunks.st: One may pledge to bring independent libations of wine,

chunks.en: but they may not give oil,
chunks.st: but one may not pledge oil alone;

chunks.en: says Rabbi Akiva.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Akiva.

chunks.en: Rabbi Tarfon says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Tarfon says:

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: They may give oil.
chunks.st: One may pledge oil as well.

chunks.en: Rabbi Tarfon said:
chunks.st: Rabbi Tarfon said:

chunks.he: מַה מָּצִינוּ בַיַּיִן שֶׁבָּא חוֹבָה וּבָא נְדָבָה,
chunks.en: Just as we find that wine comes as an obligation and comes as a gift,
chunks.st: Just as we found that wine comes as an obligation and comes as a gift offering independent of any offering,

chunks.he: אַף הַשֶּׁמֶן בָּא חוֹבָה וּבָא נְדָבָה.
chunks.en: so too oil comes as an obligation and comes as a gift.
chunks.st: so too, we find that oil comes as an obligation and comes as a gift offering.

chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva said to him:

chunks.he: לֹא, אִם אָמַרְתָּ בַיַּיִן שֶׁכֵּן הוּא
chunks.en: No! You can say this about wine, which
chunks.st: No, if you said that this is true with regard to wine, as it is

chunks.st: sacrificed with its obligatory offering

chunks.he: תֹּאמַר בַּשֶּׁמֶן שֶׁאֵינוֹ קָרֵב חוֹבָתוֹ בִפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ.
chunks.en: can you say it about oil, which is not brought by itself when it is an obligation?
chunks.st: by itself, shall you also say that this is also the case with regard to oil, which is never sacrificed with its obligatory offering by itself but only mixed with the flour?
chunks.stMore: The mishna concludes with a ruling concerning a voluntary meal offering:

chunks.en: Two people may not give one issaron together,
chunks.st: Two people do not pledge a meal offering of a tenth of an ephah as partners,

chunks.en: but they may give an olah or shelamim together.
chunks.st: but they may pledge a burnt offering and a peace offering. And

chunks.en: And with birds, even a single bird.
chunks.st: they may pledge to bring even an individual bird, not only a pair.

words.note: Usually birds are brought in pairs.
